description: Fix 1c: break the dead-end. Today a LOW-CONFIDENCE BLOCKED decision plus an UNREACHABLE client LLM (opencode has no MCP sampling) traps the run at decide: escalate() drops the fallback because of the `options.fallback.operation !== 'BLOCKED'` filter (src/autopilot/escalation.ts), so there is no path forward. When the LLM is unreachable and the model's decision is a low-confidence BLOCKED, fall back to BEST-SAFE-PROGRESS instead of trapping the run. Keep the HARD stop only for a CONFIDENT BLOCKED, the loop detector, and the destructive guard (preserve T4 safety + the no-weights graceful-BLOCKED).
steps: DESIGN THE RESOLVED DATA SHAPE FIRST (architect), THEN TDD (tdd skill). Precisely characterize the four terminal/continue cases so the fix makes illegal states unrepresentable and does not weaken safety: (1) CONFIDENT BLOCKED (operationConfidence >= gate) => still a hard stop; (2) no-weights R2 placeholder BLOCKED (loop.ts ~line 1575, source 'laya', confidence 0/0) => still degrades to graceful BLOCKED when there is genuinely no planner AND no safe progress; (3) LOW-CONFIDENCE BLOCKED + unreachable LLM => NEW best-safe-progress fallback (the bug fix); (4) loop detector / destructive guard => unchanged hard stops.

Locate the escalation dead-end in src/autopilot/escalation.ts: `escalate()` computes `const fallback = options.fallback && options.fallback.operation !== 'BLOCKED' ? options.fallback : undefined;` and, when `sample` is undefined (no sampling capability), returns a hard BLOCKED because `fallback` is undefined for a BLOCKED input. This is the exact trap.

Design a best-safe-progress resolver (prefer placing it in the loop or a small pure helper so escalation stays a thin boundary). Candidate resolution order, first that applies wins: (a) the policy layer's next sensible action for THIS page (reuse src/autopilot/policy.ts policySeed on the current PageState - the rules already know how to fill/select/submit and are the reliable path); (b) the model's highest-probability NON-BLOCKED operation above a small floor, if the engine exposed one (only if cheaply available - do not over-engineer; policySeed likely suffices for structured cases); (c) a bounded SCROLL_DOWN or WAIT-then-retry as a last safe nudge so the run makes an observable, non-destructive move rather than ending. NEVER let best-safe-progress emit a destructive CLICK - it must pass through the same destructive-form guard the loop already applies.

Implement the fix so it fires ONLY when the LLM is unreachable (no sampler, or the sampler threw/timed out) AND the decision is a LOW-CONFIDENCE BLOCKED. A CONFIDENT BLOCKED (operationConfidence >= confidenceThreshold) must NOT be rescued - that is a deliberate stop. Preserve the existing T4 behavior for a non-BLOCKED unreachable fallback (that already continues). Keep the graceful no-weights path: if there is neither a planner nor any safe progress, the run still degrades to BLOCKED (do not spin forever - the loop detector must still be able to stop it).

Wire the resolver into the loop's decision pipeline (src/autopilot/loop.ts, around the confidence-check / escalate() call ~line 1600-1620) and/or into escalate() via a new option, whichever keeps the boundary clean and escalation unit-testable via an injected function. If escalate() needs the current PageState + a policy callback to compute best-safe-progress, thread them as explicit parameters/options (do not have escalation import the loop). Update EscalationOptions/EscalationResult docs accordingly.

TDD - write these tests FIRST and watch them fail, then implement: (A) REPRODUCTION in test/escalation.test.ts (or a new test/dead-end.test.ts): a low-confidence BLOCKED decision + `sample === undefined` now PROGRESSES (resolved decision.operation !== 'BLOCKED', e.g. the policy's next action or a bounded SCROLL/WAIT) instead of returning BLOCKED. (B) a CONFIDENT BLOCKED + unreachable LLM still returns/stays BLOCKED (hard stop preserved). (C) a genuinely dead page (no policy action, no controls, no planner) still degrades to BLOCKED and the loop detector can still terminate the run (no infinite loop). (D) a loop-level test (real chromium, following the pattern in test/autopilot-autonomy-t1-t5.test.ts): a run that previously trapped at a low-confidence BLOCKED with no sampler now makes forward progress / terminates cleanly rather than dead-ending.

Confirm the existing T4 tests (test/escalation.test.ts, test/autopilot-autonomy-t1-t5.test.ts) still pass; adjust only where the new behavior intentionally changes an assertion, and explain each change in findings.
acceptance_criteria: A low-confidence BLOCKED decision with no MCP sampler resolves to a NON-BLOCKED best-safe-progress action (policy next action, else a bounded SCROLL_DOWN/WAIT) instead of a hard BLOCKED, and the run continues.
A CONFIDENT BLOCKED still hard-stops the run; the loop detector and destructive-form guard still hard-stop; a genuinely dead page still degrades to BLOCKED without looping forever.
best-safe-progress never emits a destructive CLICK (it passes the existing destructive guard) and never types/executes against a phantom ref.
New reproduction + guard tests exist and pass; existing T4 escalation/autonomy tests stay green (any intentional assertion change is justified in findings).
pnpm run typecheck clean, pnpm run build exit 0, pnpm test green.
verification: bash -lc 'pnpm test' (dead-end reproduction + guard tests pass; T4 tests stay green)
